criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use an oblique isometric view with matching diagonal ground axes.
Buildings and lattice towers share a similar pitch and upright presentation.
different: REFERENCE frames separated operational zones with more open terrain.
CANDIDATE uses a broader city-filled composition centered on a vertical river.

evidence.observation: Oblique map view shows diagonal roads, separated districts, and broad open ground.
Matching oblique projection covers a denser, river-centered city frame.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both maps contain industrial clusters, residential blocks, and extensive road texture.
Occupied regions use tightly packed small structures.
different: REFERENCE retains large rocky and smoky gaps between three main clusters.
CANDIDATE fills nearly all non-water terrain with continuous urban fabric.

evidence.observation: Large unoccupied central and upper-right areas separate industrial and residential masses.
Dense buildings and roads extend almost continuously across both riverbanks.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both show dark blue water with irregular rocky banks.
Power routes visibly approach or cross the water corridor.
different: REFERENCE has a narrow diagonal creek with subdued reflections.
CANDIDATE has a broad vertical channel with deep banks, islands, and stronger reflected light.

evidence.observation: A narrow meandering channel runs diagonally toward the lower-left edge.
A wide continuous river divides the map vertically and supports multiple crossings.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Power plants remain the largest industrial silhouettes in both views.
Transmission towers and substations have closely matched relative sizes.
different: CANDIDATE surrounds the facilities with smaller and more numerous city buildings.
The CANDIDATE upper-left plant occupies slightly more visual mass relative to nearby towers.

evidence.observation: Large plant, nearby towers, and small utility structures establish the reference scale ladder.
Central substation and adjacent lattice towers show consistent facility proportions.
Upper-left plant is dominant while nearby towers retain a comparable relative scale.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use blackened steel, charcoal concrete and soil, and restrained blue-gray midtones.
Amber window lights and cyan electrical glow share the same weathered industrial palette.
different: REFERENCE has softer blue haze and larger muted terrain patches.
CANDIDATE is sharper and more granular, with denser copper-amber highlights.

evidence.observation: Soot-dark factories, roads, rock, and sparse amber lights form a subdued material field.
The same dark industrial materials appear with finer, more numerous illuminated details.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both distinguish energized cyan conductors from dashed amber planned conductors.
Lattice towers act as readable route nodes with bright line attachments.
different: REFERENCE cyan routes are paired with multiple large translucent service-area overlays.
CANDIDATE emphasizes longer river-spanning routes and shows only a small local selection ring.

evidence.observation: Glowing cyan lines connect plants, towers, and substations across the upper map.
Amber towers and dashed conductors clearly denote a planned lower route.
Cyan energized and amber planned networks remain distinct across both riverbanks.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use riveted black industrial chrome around the top, left kit, and right inspector.
Cyan and amber accents consistently separate power and status information.
different: CANDIDATE has denser labeling, a taller inspector, and a full-width lower overlay.
REFERENCE uses a compact inspector, mostly icon-led kit, and a small centered playback panel.

evidence.observation: Segmented chrome top bar presents budget, power, day, and pause state.
Compact right inspector prioritizes one facility image, capacity bar, and two actions.
Taller inspector adds multiple labeled status rows beneath the facility summary.

criteria.label: WEAK
similar: Both place dark chrome process controls along the bottom edge.
Both reuse cyan selection and amber status accents.
different: REFERENCE shows only a compact playback-speed controller.
CANDIDATE shows an independent full-width event-stage bar with briefing, planning, progress, connection, result, and next-stage states.

evidence.observation: Bottom panel contains reverse, play, and speed controls without event stages or results.
Full-width staged flow includes event count, current stage, construction progress, result, and next-stage control.
